newsitem.title: USA: Boeing CEO Condit to become chairman.
newsitem.headline: Boeing CEO Condit to become chairman.

text.p: Boeing Co. Chairman Frank Shrontz will retire as of Jan. 31, making way for Chief Executive Officer Phil Condit to take on the additional title, the company said Monday.
Shrontz gave up the chief executive's title in April after 10 years in the post and said then that he planned to step down as chairman shortly after he turned 65, which he does this week.
Condit, 55, an engineer credited with leading the effort to design and build Boeing's new 777 jetliner, joined the world's biggest airplane manufacturer in 1965 and has been president since 1992.
He is the seventh executive to lead the 80-year-old company.
Condit will continue to handle the duties of company president, although that title will be left vacant.
Shrontz will continue as a member of Boeing's board of directors as chairman emeritus.
